    −15  Redis is open to the internet on port 6379

  Every finding, with its fix: sudo kiyesi scan

  Kiyesi can fix 1 thing for you:

  1. /opt/appstack/.env.api holds secrets and every user on this server can read it (secret-files)
     Makes 1 file unreadable to other users on this server; its owner and group keep access: /opt/appstack/.env.api.

  Left to you (1):

  • SSH allows root login (ssh-root)  +5, to D 55, when done
    You are signed in as root, so turning root login off now could lock you out. Password login is already off, so root can sign in only with its key.
    To turn root login off safely, as root, with your own name for <you>:
      1. Check root's keys, and take out any nobody recognises:
           sudo kiyesi keys
           sudo kiyesi keys remove <fingerprint>
      2. Make your own user, able to use sudo:
           adduser <you> && usermod -aG sudo <you>
      3. Give it only your own key, never a copy of root's authorized_keys. On your
         own computer, cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub; then here, with that one line:
           install -d -m 700 -o <you> -g <you> /home/<you>/.ssh
           echo 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@laptop' > /home/<you>/.ssh/authorized_keys
           chown <you>: /home/<you>/.ssh/authorized_keys && chmod 600 /home/<you>/.ssh/authorized_keys
      4. Keep this session open. From a new terminal: ssh <you>@this-server, then sudo -v
      5. Only when both work, signed in as <you>: sudo kiyesi fix ssh-root
